name: Ann Briggs

nadir.desc: The property consists of a large primary residence with a tan roof covered by multiple solar panel arrays|Several vehicles are parked in the driveway and parking area near the house|Dense mature trees surround much of the structure on all sides|A paved driveway provides access from the street|Open ground and landscaped areas are present between the trees and the building.

alpha.desc: The front of the residence is largely screened by dense tall evergreen trees|Portions of the tan roof and solar panel arrays are visible through the vegetation|Multiple vehicles are parked in the driveway area|Street access is present along the front of the property|The house sits within a heavily wooded lot.

bravo.desc: The left side of the residence shows dense tall trees dominating the view|Portions of the house roof and solar panels are visible through the tree cover|A paved walking path goes towards the backyard|Vehicles are parked near the driveway|The street runs along the lower edge of the property|Limited open space exists between the trees and the structure.

charlie.desc: The rear of the residence is heavily screened by dense tall evergreen trees|Portions of the roof are visible through the canopy|Open ground and tree cover extend across the rear of the lot|Clear views of the building walls are limited by the vegetation density.

delta.desc: The right side of the residence shows dense tall trees with portions of the house, solar panels, and driveway area visible through the canopy|A path is present at the edge of the property|The structure remains partially obscured by the surrounding tree cover.

considerations: Vehicle access is provided by a paved driveway that leads from the street into a parking area near the house. Multiple vehicles are parked in the driveway. Dense mature trees surround the property on all sides and significantly limit visibility and open movement around the structure. Solar panel arrays cover large sections of the roof. The property is located on a residential court adjacent to a golf course, with neighboring homes nearby. Open ground exists in limited pockets between the trees and the building.
clarifications: How dense is the tree cover for emergency vehicle and pedestrian movement around all sides of the house? Does the driveway provide adequate turnaround space given the number of parked vehicles? Are there any secondary access points or paths through the tree cover to the rear of the property? What is the clearance between the solar panel arrays and the roof edges for potential roof access? Is the property fully enclosed by fencing, or do open paths exist between neighboring lots?
